walkthroughs.body_html:
V = I × R can be rearranged three ways. 🔌

To find current: I = V ÷ R. To find resistance: R = V ÷ I. Cover the letter you want — the other two tell you what to do.

Check units every time: V in volts, I in amperes, R in ohms.

Q = I × t connects charge to current. Charge Q is in coulombs (C), current I in amperes, time t in seconds.

Example: a current of 2 A for 5 s moves 10 C of charge.

Always convert minutes to seconds before plugging in. 60 s in a minute — easy slip if you forget.

In series: current is the same everywhere, voltages add, resistances add.

In parallel: each branch has the same voltage as the supply, and the branch currents add to give the total.

Voltage divider: two equal series resistors split the supply voltage in half.

mcqs.q: A 6 V supply pushes a current of 0.5 A through a resistor. What is the resistance?
options: 3 Ω

mcqs.q: Two identical 10 Ω resistors are in series across a 12 V supply. What is the voltage across each?
options: 6 V
3 V

mcqs.q: What happens to the total resistance when you add another resistor in parallel?
options: Current splits in half at the battery so each direction gets some.
Adding a parallel resistor doubles the voltage available.
Adding any resistor always increases the total resistance.
Total resistance decreases — there are more paths for current to flow.

mcqs.q: What happens to the current as it goes around a series circuit?
options: Adding a parallel resistor doubles the voltage available.
Current splits in half at the battery so each direction gets some.
It stays the same at every point — current is conserved.
Current gets used up by each component as it flows around the circuit.

mcqs.q: What does voltage (potential difference) across a component represent?
options: Voltage measures how many electrons are stored in a battery.
Voltage is the 'amount of electricity' flowing through the wire.
The energy transferred per unit charge passing through that component.
Current splits in half at the battery so each direction gets some.

options: Same voltage on each branch; currents add
Unit of electric charge, symbol C
Same current; voltages add; resistances add
Two series resistors split voltage in their ratio

options: Charge (C) equals current (A) times time (s)
